definition: DistinctCause cause x requires a c unequal to x satisfying the independently supplied relation cause c x. Distinctness does not require that c be outside the parts of x. In the omission model the relation is strict parthood, not an asserted actual efficient-cause or grounding law.
note: Analyst scope profile for #328, motivated by the materialized Varzi exposition. All-subset quantification is an explicit second-order mathematical choice; neither causal sufficiency nor metaphysical adequacy is attributed to the source. See docs/notes/universal-fusion-grounding.md.
